description: Confidential computing decomposed. TEE architectures: Intel SGX (deprecated), Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP, ARM CCA. Memory encryption + attestation + isolation. Confidential VMs in cloud (AWS Nitro, Azure CVM, GCP CVM). Use cases: data at rest, data in use, multi-party compute.

sub_mechanisms.name: TEE_isolation_boundary
sub_mechanisms.definition: Hardware-enforced separation between trusted code/data and host OS/hypervisor.
sub_mechanisms.why: Even compromised host OS can't read TEE memory. Different from VMs (host sees encrypted RAM). Fundamental confidential computing property.

sub_mechanisms.name: Intel_SGX_enclave
sub_mechanisms.definition: Process-level TEE. App marks portions as enclave; CPU enforces isolation. Limited memory (~128 MB enclave).
sub_mechanisms.why: First widespread TEE (2015). Side-channel issues (Foreshadow, Spectre derivatives). Deprecated in client CPUs 2021. Server SGX continues.

sub_mechanisms.name: Intel_TDX_VM
sub_mechanisms.definition: Trust Domain Extensions. VM-level TEE replacing SGX. Encrypted VMs invisible to hypervisor.
sub_mechanisms.why: Whole-VM model simpler than enclave model. Larger memory. AWS, Azure, GCP deploying. Modern Intel confidential computing default.

sub_mechanisms.name: AMD_SEV_SNP
sub_mechanisms.definition: Secure Encrypted Virtualization - Secure Nested Paging. VM-level encryption + integrity. AMD EPYC.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cloud confidential VMs. SEV-SNP adds integrity protection over original SEV. Production-ready (3rd gen EPYC).

sub_mechanisms.name: ARM_CCA
sub_mechanisms.definition: Confidential Compute Architecture. ARMv9 extension. Realm-based isolation.
sub_mechanisms.why: ARM's TEE story beyond TrustZone. Production deployment 2024+. Cloud + edge confidential computing.

sub_mechanisms.name: memory_encryption_keys
sub_mechanisms.definition: CPU encrypts memory writes with per-VM/enclave key. Decrypts on read. Key never leaves CPU.
sub_mechanisms.why: Physical attacker (DIMM probe) gets ciphertext only. Host OS reading TEE memory gets garbage. Hardware root of trust.

sub_mechanisms.name: remote_attestation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Hardware-signed proof of: what code is running, what config, what hash. Verifier validates signature + content.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of confidential computing trust. Without attestation, can't verify what's actually executing. Critical: don't trust client's claim — trust signed measurement.

sub_mechanisms.name: TEE_attestation_chain
sub_mechanisms.definition: Chain: TEE → CPU manufacturer (Intel/AMD) → root certificate. Proves TEE genuine + measurement correct.
sub_mechanisms.why: Trust anchored in hardware vendor. Manufacturer signs CPU's attestation key. Verifier walks chain to verified root. Standard PKI-style verification.

sub_mechanisms.name: side_channel_vulnerabilities
sub_mechanisms.definition: TEE leaks information via timing, cache, power, EM. Spectre, Foreshadow, ZombieLoad.
sub_mechanisms.why: Ongoing concern. Each CPU generation patches discovered channels. Confidential computing trades hardware trust for software trust. Side channels are TEEs' main weakness.

sub_mechanisms.name: confidential_VM_cloud
sub_mechanisms.definition: Cloud VM where customer data + code invisible to cloud provider. AWS Nitro, Azure CVM (TDX/SEV), GCP CVM.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cloud regulatory + trust use case. Healthcare, finance, government workloads. Customer doesn't trust cloud provider; CVM gives cryptographic isolation.

sub_mechanisms.name: multi_party_compute_TEE
sub_mechanisms.definition: Multiple parties contribute encrypted data; TEE computes; only result revealed.
sub_mechanisms.why: Joint analytics without sharing raw data. Healthcare consortia, financial fraud detection. Alternative to cryptographic MPC (faster but trust hardware).

sub_mechanisms.name: confidential_AI_inference
sub_mechanisms.definition: Model weights + user data both confidential. Used for privacy-preserving LLM inference.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cloud inference exposing user prompts to provider. Confidential VMs run inference; provider sees only ciphertext. Apple Private Cloud Compute uses this pattern.

derivation_rules.name: TEE_protects_data_in_use
then: host operator can't read or modify it
derivation_rules.why: Memory encrypted with key only TEE knows. Different from at-rest encryption (decrypted in RAM normally). Different from in-transit (decrypted on receive). The 'in use' protection.

derivation_rules.name: attestation_required_for_trust
if: a relying party connects to a TEE
then: it must verify attestation before sending sensitive data
derivation_rules.why: Without attestation: malicious endpoint claiming to be TEE. With attestation: cryptographic proof of TEE genuine + running expected code. Foundation of TEE deployment patterns.

derivation_rules.name: side_channels_continue_to_emerge
if: a TEE has been deployed at scale
then: new side channels will be discovered over time
derivation_rules.why: Each TEE generation has discovered channels (Spectre/Meltdown/Foreshadow/MDS for Intel; many SEV bypasses). Mitigations patched but new ones found. TEEs are ongoing arms race.

derivation_rules.name: confidential_VM_easier_than_enclave
if: application is a normal VM workload
then: confidential VM model (TDX, SEV-SNP) easier than enclave (SGX)
derivation_rules.why: SGX requires app refactor: enclave / non-enclave split. CVM: existing VM image works. Modern cloud confidential computing trends toward CVM model.

derivation_rules.name: TEE_changes_trust_model_in_cloud
then: cloud provider not in customer's trust boundary
derivation_rules.why: Without CVM: provider has full access (debug, ops, support). With CVM: provider sees encrypted memory only. Regulated industries (healthcare, finance) increasingly require this.
